topic.para: On &suselinux; 15, Go is updated inside released Service Packs rather than only at Service Pack boundaries.

listitem.para: Releases are kept in sync with upstream, which nominally occur every 6 months in February and August.
&suse; maintains versions N and N-1, mirroring the upstream support policy. Minor releases are made available shortly after the upstream release.
Different versions are parallel installable and undergo automated testing. The go metapackage always points to the latest go1.x package.
Go is supported across both the General Support and the LTSS phases.

topic.para: When building applications, you have two options regarding versions:

listitem.para: To build with the latest recommended version, let the application depend on BuildRequires: golang(API) >= go1.23.
To control the timing of build changes, pin the application to a specific go1.x package using BuildRequires: golang(API) == go1.23.

topic.para: In both cases, you must use the major version of go1.x specified in the application's go.mod file, as the Go compiler requires this as a minimum version.

Alongside the regular go1.xx packages, &suse; ships a parallel go1.xx-openssl variant that enables FIPS-compliant Go applications. Two -openssl versions are supported at any time, but they follow their own release cycle, shifted by a few weeks from the regular packages. Keep two -openssl versions available when you depend on them.
